episode_title: The Future of Classic Cars | David Dyer and The Modern Classic Car Foundation

real_qa.q: What apprenticeship trades does the Modern Classic Car Foundation offer to young people?
real_qa.r: The Modern Classic Car Foundation currently offers training in four main trades: paint and panel work, live vehicle mechanics, auto electrical work, and trimming. They are also working to establish engine machining training, which has been difficult to set up, and plan to add motorbike training later in the year. Apprentices are employed by the foundation, attend standard TAFE training, and work in a 'man and boy' mentorship scheme where they are paired with experienced tradespeople.
real_qa.requete: Modern Classic Car Foundation apprenticeships trades

real_qa.q: How many apprentices does the Modern Classic Car Foundation currently employ and what are the growth plans?
real_qa.r: The Modern Classic Car Foundation currently has five apprentices and plans to grow to between 10 and 15 apprentices at their current Bankstown Airport location. The long-term plan is to replicate the foundation model around Australia so they can reach talent pools beyond the one-hour drive radius of their Sydney base.
real_qa.requete: Modern Classic Car Foundation apprentices growth expansion

real_qa.q: What is the average build cost for a restored classic car at the Modern Classic Car Foundation?
real_qa.r: Build costs at the Modern Classic Car Foundation average between $200,000 and $300,000 per vehicle. These cars are essentially new vehicles with old-school looks and all modern conveniences and performance, positioned as an alternative to buying production-made sports cars. The pricing is considered reasonable compared to restomod prices around the world.
real_qa.requete: Modern Classic Car Foundation restomod build cost price

real_qa.q: What is the financial sustainability model of the Modern Classic Car Foundation?
real_qa.r: The Modern Classic Car Foundation is approximately 70% self-sufficient from the restoration work it performs, with the remaining 30% needing to come from donations of vehicles, government grants, and help from organizations. The foundation is not profitable and operates at a financial loss, requiring ongoing external support to sustain its training and restoration operations.
real_qa.requete: Modern Classic Car Foundation funding financial model

real_qa.q: What specific classic car restorations has the Modern Classic Car Foundation completed?
real_qa.r: The Modern Classic Car Foundation specializes in MGs with a standard platform for MGAs and MGBs fitted with Mazda engines, air conditioning, central locking, and power steering. Recent and ongoing projects include a 1980s G-Class Mercedes with a 6.2-litre LS engine, Lotus models, a 1980s Toyota Land Cruiser, and a 1959 MGA Twin Cam with a 2.5-litre Mazda Ford engine. The foundation currently has around 30 cars from 14 different brands in-house.
real_qa.requete: Modern Classic Car Foundation car restoration projects MG Lotus

guest.bio_context: David Dwyer studied mechanical engineering with a specialty in automotive and electrical design, and ran a successful car restoration business that grew to 12 employees before he decided to convert it into a charitable foundation. About 18 months before this interview, his family donated the business to form the Modern Classic Car Foundation as a charitable trust. He has a lifelong passion for classic cars inherited from his British father, who owned MGs and Jaguars, and still owns a 1953 MG TD that he and his father restored together.

real_quote: They've revitalised me. They've revitalised the company, if you can call it that. Young people have inquisitive minds and blow my mind with what they impart back.
